exposure: Presence of ISUA (ISUA vs. three-vessel cord)
outcome: Emergency cesarean delivery rate due to fetal factors
cohort: 93,592 pregnant women with singleton pregnancy, full-term birth, and no known fetal chromosomal and structural anomalies, who gave birth between January 2011 and January 2012 in 39 hospitals within China
finding: Infants born to mothers with an ISUA had significantly lower birth weight, birth length, placental weight, umbilical cord length, and Apgar scores at 1 minute, and a higher incidence of SGA and LBW, but ISUA was not associated with a decreased rate of vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: While an isolated single umbilical artery (ISUA) was associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, it did not decrease the rate of vaginal delivery in full-term births.
birth_weight: Research group: 3264.71 ± 469.95 g, Comparison group: 3340.76 ± 434.25 g
